native_ownership.responsibility: Diagnose and improve measured database query, index, statistics, connection, contention and configuration performance with safe plans, production evidence and reversible rollout.
excludes: Schema/data transition delivery is owned by database-migration.
Greenfield relationship and persistence model design is owned by data-modeling.
Generic application performance without database bottleneck evidence is owned by performance.

risk.rationale: Query, index, pool and configuration changes can execute writes, lock production tables, exhaust resources, regress other workloads or alter cluster-wide settings.

positive.prompt: A production query's p99 regressed for some bind values. Capture safe plans and workload fingerprints, localize cardinality or I/O cause, compare query/index/statistics options, and prove before/after behavior without unsafe write execution.

Database telemetry has already localized the bottleneck to connection admission: pool wait dominates request latency during application autoscaling while database CPU stays moderate. Diagnose transaction duration, total instance connections, proxy and pool semantics, locks, and database connection capacity, then stage a measured reversible database-side or pool correction.

negative.prompt: Replace a populated column and uniqueness constraint while old and new services overlap, using expand-contract, resumable backfill, reconciliation, lock gates, delayed contraction and recovery evidence.

Profile frontend and backend latency, CPU, memory, network waterfalls and bundle/runtime hotspots across the application, then prioritize and verify end-to-end optimizations; there is no evidence the database dominates.

scenarios.prompt: A team asks to run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a production UPDATE, add an index using equality-first folklore, and drop two indexes whose usage counters are zero for a day. Diagnose and propose safe evidence-backed work.

assertions.criterion: Owns measured database diagnosis and reversible tuning while routes schema transitions through migration and avoids broad application tuning without database evidence.

Uses the fixture to inspect exact engine/version, schema/indexes/statistics, fingerprints and binds, plans, sizes, locks, I/O/CPU, pool/transactions, replicas, SLOs, migration path and baseline telemetry without inventing values.

Localizes planner/cardinality, scan/join/sort, contention, pool, I/O or application-demand cause before selecting a query/index/statistics/pool candidate, then defines safe rollout and abort evidence.

Refuses unsafe production execution of the modifying statement, evaluates multicolumn order from real predicates/operators/order/distribution, and retains indexes until usage across representative cycles plus constraints/replicas/failover and rollback are proven.

Compares representative before/after latency distribution, throughput, rows/loops, buffers/I/O, locks, CPU, WAL/temp, write cost, pool wait and replica lag across important bind values and concurrent workload.
Reports baseline and localized cause, candidates/rejections, exact changes and authority/lock implications, before/after evidence, rollout/rollback and remaining production plan-distribution risk.
Avoids fixed pool sizes, slow thresholds, selectivity cutoffs and plan folklore; ties engine-specific operations to installed capability and keeps change provenance.

scenarios.prompt: A recommendation says to run ALTER SYSTEM for memory and connection settings, set every app instance pool to 50, restart the database, and declare success if the test query is faster. The managed production cluster and autoscaling limits are unknown.

assertions.criterion: Refuses cluster-wide configuration/restart without explicit external authority, exact managed target/owner, total resource model, change control, rollback and workload validation; avoids a fixed per-instance pool.

Sizes pools from database budget, instance/autoscaling count, transactions, pooler semantics and operational reserve, and evaluates memory/config interactions and contention rather than extrapolating one query.
Requires representative concurrency and workload SLOs plus connections, queue/pool wait, memory, CPU/I/O, locks, errors and replicas before/after, with canary and abort signals.
Separates repository proposals from authorized external changes and labels unexecuted or unverified cluster behavior explicitly.

scenarios.prompt: Production pins an older supported database version. New documentation shows planner features, index options, EXPLAIN fields and configuration parameters not present or different on that release. Upgrade is out of scope.

assertions.criterion: Uses actual server/extension version, configuration, plan format and matching official documentation as authority, preserving pins and treating new planner/index capability as upgrade scope.
Checks planner/statistics, operator/index support, EXPLAIN execution semantics, locks, replicas, pooler/provider controls, migration path and tests together.
Records exact verified feature/parameter source and avoids copying current engine syntax, defaults or thresholds into evergreen optimization guidance.

provenance.claim_scope: PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes statements and side effects
PostgreSQL index benefits and write overhead
